paragraphs.sourceText: Questions 26 to 35 are based on the following passage.
paragraphs.translationZh: 第 26 至 35 题基于以下段落。

paragraphs.sourceText: It is important that scientists be seen as normal people asking and answering important questions. Good, sound science depends on 26 , experiments and reasoned methodologies. It requires a willingness to ask new questions and try new approaches. It requires one to take risks and experience failures. But good science also requires 27 understanding, clear explanation and concise presentation.
paragraphs.translationZh: 重要的是，科学家应该被视为提出和回答重要问题的普通人。良好、可靠的科学依赖于假设、实验和合理的方法。它需要愿意提出新问题并尝试新方法。它需要一个人承担风险并经历失败。但好的科学还需要上下文理解、清晰的解释和简洁的表达。

paragraphs.sourceText: Our country needs more scientists who are willing to step out in the public 28 and offer their opinions on important matters. We need more scientists who can explain what they are doing in language that is 29 and understandable to the public. Those of us who are not scientists should also be prepared to support public engagement by scientists, and to 30 scientific knowledge into our public communications.
paragraphs.translationZh: 我们的国家需要更多愿意走出公共舞台，就重大问题发表意见的科学家。我们需要更多的科学家能够用令人信服且易于公众理解的语言解释他们正在做的事情。我们这些不是科学家的人也应该准备好支持科学家的公众参与，并将科学知识纳入我们的公共传播中。

paragraphs.sourceText: Too many people in this country, including some among our elected leadership, still do not understand how science works or why robust, long-range investments in research vitally matter. In the 1960s, the United States 31
paragraphs.translationZh: 这个国家有太多人，包括我们选出的领导层中的一些人，仍然不明白科学是如何运作的，也不明白为什么对研究进行强有力的长期投资至关重要。 20世纪60年代，美国致力于

paragraphs.sourceText: nearly 17% of discretionary (可酌情支配的) spending to research and development, 32 decades of economic growth. By 2008, the figure had fallen into the single 33 This occurs at a time when other nations have made significant gains in their own research capabilities.
paragraphs.translationZh: 近17%的可自由支配支出用于研发，收获了数十年的经济增长。到 2008 年，这一数字已降至个位数。此时，其他国家的研究能力已取得显着进步。

paragraphs.sourceText: At the University of California (UC), we 34 ourselves not only on the quality of our research, but also on its contribution to improving our world. To 35 the development of science from the lab bench to the market place, UC is investing our own money in our own good ideas.
paragraphs.translationZh: 在加州大学 (UC)，我们不仅为我们的研究质量感到自豪，也为我们为改善世界做出的贡献而感到自豪。为了加速科学从实验室走向市场的发展，加州大学正在将自己的资金投入到我们自己的好想法中。

paragraphs.sourceText: Directions: In this section, you are going to read a passage with ten statements attached to it. Each statement contains information given in one of the paragraphs. Identify the paragraph from which the information is derived. You may choose a paragraph more than once. Each paragraph is marked with a letter. Answer the questions by marking the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet 2.
paragraphs.translationZh: 说明：在本节中，您将阅读一段附有十个陈述的段落。每条陈述都包含其中一个段落中给出的信息。确定信息来源的段落。您可以多次选择一个段落。每个段落都标有一个字母。通过在答题卡 2 上标记相应的字母来回答问题。

paragraphs.sourceText: Are We in an Innovation Lull?
paragraphs.translationZh: 我们正处于创新停滞期吗？

paragraphs.sourceText: A. Scan the highlights of this year's Consumer Electronics Show ( CES ), and you may get a slight feeling of having seen them before. Many of the coolest gadgets this year are the same as the coolest gadgets last year--or the year before, even. The booths are still exciting, and the demos are still just as crazy. It is still easy to be dazzled by the display of drones (无人机),3D printers, virtual reality goggles ( 眼镜) and more "smart" devices than you could ever hope to catalog. Upon reflection, however, it is equally easy to feel like you have seen it all before. And it is hard not to think: Are we in an innovation lull ( 间歇期) ?
paragraphs.translationZh: A. 浏览今年消费电子展（CES）的亮点，你可能会有一丝似曾相识的感觉。今年许多最酷的小玩意与去年甚至前年最酷的小玩意相同。展位仍然令人兴奋，演示仍然同样疯狂。无人机、3D 打印机、虚拟现实护目镜和更多超乎你想象的“智能”设备的展示仍然很容易让人眼花缭乱。然而，经过反思，你同样很容易感觉这一切都已经见过了。人们很难不去思考：我们是否正处于创新间歇期？

paragraphs.sourceText: B. In some ways, the answer is yes. For years, smartphones, televisions, tablets, laptops and desktops have made up a huge part of the market and driven innovation. But now these segments are looking at slower growth curves--or shrinking markets in some cases--as consumers are not as eager to spend money on new gadgets. Meanwhile, emerging technologies--the drones,3D printers and smart-home devices of the world--now seem a bit too old to be called "the next big thing. "
paragraphs.translationZh: B. 从某些方面来说，答案是肯定的。多年来，智能手机、电视、平板电脑、笔记本电脑和台式机占据了市场的很大一部分，并推动了创新。但现在这些细分市场的增长曲线正在放缓，或者在某些情况下市场正在萎缩，因为消费者不再那么渴望花钱购买新产品。与此同时，世界各地的新兴技术——无人机、3D打印机和智能家居设备——现在似乎有点太老了，无法被称为“下一个重大技术”。

paragraphs.sourceText: C. Basically the tech industry seems to be in an awkward period now. "There is not any one-hit wonder, and there will not be one for years to come," said Gary Shapiro, president and chief executive of the Consumer Technology Association (CTA). In his eyes, however, that doesn't necessarily mean that innovation has stopped. It has just grown up a little. "Many industries are going out of infancy and becoming adolescents," Shapiro said.
paragraphs.translationZh: C. 基本上科技行业现在似乎处于一个尴尬的时期。消费者技术协会 (CTA) 主席兼首席执行官加里·夏皮罗 (Gary Shapiro) 表示：“不存在一击即成的奇迹，而且在未来几年内也不会有这样的奇迹。”然而，在他看来，这并不一定意味着创新已经停止。它刚刚长大了一点。 “许多行业正在走出婴儿期，进入青少年期，”夏皮罗说。

paragraphs.sourceText: D. For instance, new technologies that are building upon existing technology have not found their footing well enough to appeal to a mass audience, because, in many cases, they need to work effectively with other devices to realize their full appeal. Take the evolution of the smart home, for example. Companies are pushing it hard but make it almost overwhelming even to dip a toe in the water for the average consumer, because there are so many compatibility issues to think about. No average person wants to figure out whether their favorite calendar software works with their fridge or whether their washing machine and tablet get along. Having to install a different app for each smart appliance in your home is annoying; it would be nicer if you could manage everything together. And while you may forgive your smartphone an occasional fault, you probably have less patience for error messages from your door lock.
paragraphs.translationZh: D. 例如，基于现有技术的新技术尚未站稳脚跟，无法吸引大众，因为在许多情况下，它们需要与其他设备有效配合才能充分发挥其吸引力。以智能家居的发展为例。公司正在大力推动这一举措，但对于普通消费者来说，即使是尝试一下也几乎难以承受，因为有太多的兼容性问题需要考虑。没有一个普通人想知道他们最喜欢的日历软件是否适用于他们的冰箱，或者他们的洗衣机和平板电脑是否兼容。必须为家中的每个智能设备安装不同的应用程序是很烦人的；如果你们能一起管理所有事情就更好了。虽然您可能会原谅智能手机偶尔出现的故障，但您可能对门锁发出的错误消息缺乏耐心。

paragraphs.sourceText: E. Companies are promoting their own standards, and the market has not had time to choose a winner yet as this is still very new. Companies that have long focused on hardware now have to think of ecosystems instead to give consumers practical solutions to their everyday problems."The dialogue is changing from what is technologically possible to what is technologically meaningful," said economist Shawn DuBravac. DuBravac works for CTA--which puts on the show each year--and said that this shift to a search for solutions has been noticeable as he researched his predictions for 2016.
paragraphs.translationZh: E. 公司正在推广自己的标准，市场还没有时间选择赢家，因为这仍然是一个非常新的标准。长期专注于硬件的公司现在必须考虑生态系统，而不是为消费者提供解决日常问题的实用解决方案。“对话正在从技术上可行转向技术上有意义，”经济学家肖恩·杜布拉瓦克说。杜布拉瓦茨 (DuBravac) 为每年都会举办该节目的 CTA 工作，他表示，在他研究 2016 年的预测时，这种寻求解决方案的转变已经很明显。

paragraphs.sourceText: F. "So much of what CES has been about is the cool. It is about the flashiness and the gadgets," said John Curran, managing director of research at Accenture. "But over the last couple of years, and in this one in particular, we are starting to see companies shift from what is the largest screen size, the smallest form factor or the shiniest object and more into what all of these devices do that is practical in a consumer's life. " Even the technology press conferences, which have been high- profile in the past and reached a level of drama and theatrics fitting for a Las Vegas stage, have a different bent to them. Rather than just dazzling with a high cool factor, there is a focus on the practical. Fitbit, for example, released its first smartwatch Monday, selling with a clear purpose--to improve your fitness--and promoting it as a "tool, not a toy. " Not only that, it supports a number of platforms: Apple's iOS, Google's Android and Microsoft's Windows phone.
paragraphs.translationZh: F. 埃森哲研究部董事总经理约翰·柯兰 (John Curran) 表示：“CES 的主题大多是炫酷。它是关于华丽和小玩意的。” “但在过去的几年里，尤其是在这几年，我们开始看到公司从最大的屏幕尺寸、最小的外形尺寸或最闪亮的物体转向所有这些设备在消费者生活中的实用功能。”即使是过去备受瞩目、达到了适合拉斯维加斯舞台的戏剧性水平的技术新闻发布会，也有了不同的倾向。不仅仅是炫酷的炫酷元素，更注重实用性。例如，Fitbit 周一发布了首款智能手表，其销售目的很明确——改善健康——并将其宣传为“工具，而不是玩具”。不仅如此，它还支持多种平台：苹果的 iOS、谷歌的 Android 和微软的 Windows 手机。

paragraphs.sourceText: G. That seems to be what consumers are demanding, after all. Consumers are becoming increasingly bored with what companies have to offer: A survey of 28,000 consumers in 28 countries released by Accenture found consumers are not as excited about technology as they once were. For example, when asked whether they would buy a new smartphone this year, only 48 percent said yes--a six-point drop from 2015.
paragraphs.translationZh: G. 毕竟，这似乎正是消费者的要求。消费者对公司提供的产品越来越感到厌倦：埃森哲发布的一项针对 28 个国家 28,000 名消费者的调查发现，消费者对技术不再像以前那样兴奋。例如，当被问及今年是否会购买新智能手机时，只有 48% 的人表示愿意，比 2015 年下降了 6 个百分点。

paragraphs.sourceText: H. And when it comes to the hyper-connected super-smart world that technology firms are painting for us, it seems that consumers are growing more uneasy about handing over the massive amounts of consumer data needed to provide the personalized, customized solutions that companies need to improve their services. That could be another explanation for why companies seem to be strengthening their talk of the practicality of their devices.
paragraphs.translationZh: H.当谈到科技公司正在为我们描绘的超连接的超级智能世界时，消费者似乎越来越不安于交出大量的消费者数据，这些数据是公司改善服务所需的个性化、定制的解决方案。这可能是为什么公司似乎在加强对其设备实用性的谈论的另一种解释。

paragraphs.sourceText: I. Companies have already won part of the battle, having driven tech into every part of our lives, tracking our steps and our very heartbeats. Yet the persistent question of " Why do I need that?"--or, perhaps more tellingly, "Why do you need to know that?"--dogs the steps of many new ventures. Only 13 percent of respondents said that they were interested in buying a smartwatch in 2016, for example--an increase of just one percent from the previous year despite a year of high-profile launches. That is bad news for any firm that may hope that smartwatches can make up ground for maturing smartphone and tablet markets. And the survey found flat demand for fitness monitors, smart thermostats (恒温器) and connected home cameras, as well.
paragraphs.translationZh: I. 公司已经赢得了这场战斗的部分胜利，将科技带入我们生活的方方面面，追踪我们的脚步和心跳。然而，“为什么我需要这个？”——或者也许更能说明问题的是，“为什么你需要知道这个？”这个持续存在的问题困扰着许多新企业的脚步。例如，只有 13% 的受访者表示他们有兴趣在 2016 年购买智能手表，尽管这一年发布的智能手表备受瞩目，但这一比例仅比前一年增加了 1%。对于任何希望智能手表能够弥补成熟的智能手机和平板电脑市场的公司来说，这都是一个坏消息。调查发现，健身监视器、智能恒温器和联网家用摄像头的需求也持平。

paragraphs.sourceText: J. According to the survey, that lack of enthusiasm could stem from concerns about privacy and security. Even among people who have bought connected devices of some kind,37 percent said that they are going to be more cautions about using these devices and services in the future. A full 18 percent have even returned devices until they feel they can get safer guarantees against having their sensitive information hacked.
paragraphs.translationZh: J. 根据调查，缺乏热情可能源于对隐私和安全的担忧。即使在购买了某种联网设备的人中，37% 的人也表示，他们将来在使用这些设备和服务时会更加谨慎。整整 18% 的人甚至退回了设备，直到他们觉得可以获得更安全的保证，防止敏感信息被黑客攻击。

paragraphs.sourceText: K. That, too, explains the heavy Washington presence at this year's show, as these new technologies intrude upon heavily regulated areas. In addition to many senior officials from the Federal Trade and Federal Communications commissions, this year's list of policy makers also includes appearances from Transportation Secretary Anthony Foxx, to talk about smart cities, and Federal Aviation Administration Administrator Michael Huerta, to talk about drones.
paragraphs.translationZh: K. 这也解释了华盛顿在今年展会上的大量亮相，因为这些新技术侵入了严格监管的领域。除了来自联邦贸易和联邦通信委员会的许多高级官员外，今年的政策制定者名单还包括交通部长安东尼·福克斯（Anthony Foxx）和联邦航空管理局局长迈克尔·韦尔塔（Michael Huerta），他们将出席讨论智慧城市，讨论无人机。

paragraphs.sourceText: L. Curran, the Accenture analyst, said that increased government interest in the show makes sense as technology becomes a larger part of our lives. "There is an incompatibility in the rate at which these are advancing relative to the way we're digesting it," he said. "Technology is becoming bigger and more aspirational, and penetrating almost every aspect of our lives. We have to understand and think about the implications, and balance these great innovations with the potential downsides they naturally carry with them. "
paragraphs.translationZh: 埃森哲分析师 L. Curran 表示，随着技术成为我们生活的重要组成部分，政府对展会的兴趣增加是有道理的。 “这些进展的速度与我们消化它的方式不相容，”他说。 “技术正在变得越来越大、越来越令人向往，几乎渗透到我们生活的方方面面。我们必须理解和思考其影响，并平衡这些伟大的创新与它们自然带来的潜在缺点。”

paragraphs.sourceText: 36. Consumers are often hesitant to try smart-home devices because they are worried about compatibility problems.
paragraphs.translationZh: 36. 消费者常常犹豫是否尝试智能家居设备，因为他们担心兼容性问题。

paragraphs.sourceText: 37. This year's electronics show featured the presence of many officials from the federal government.
paragraphs.translationZh: 37. 今年的电子展有许多联邦政府官员出席。

paragraphs.sourceText: 38. The market demand for electronic devices is now either declining or not growing as fast as before.
paragraphs.translationZh: 38. 电子设备的市场需求现在要么下降，要么增长速度不如以前。

paragraphs.sourceText: 39. One analyst suggests it is necessary to accept both the positive and negative aspects of innovative products.
paragraphs.translationZh: 39. 一位分析师认为，有必要接受创新产品的积极和消极方面。

paragraphs.sourceText: 40. The Consumer Electronics Show in recent years has begun to focus more on the practical value than the showiness of electronic devices.
paragraphs.translationZh: 40. 近年来的消费电子展开始更加注重电子设备的实用价值而不是炫耀。

paragraphs.sourceText: 41. Fewer innovative products were found at this year's electronic products show.
paragraphs.translationZh: 41. 今年电子产品展的创新产品较少。

paragraphs.sourceText: 42. Consumers are becoming more worried about giving personal information to tech companies to get customized products and services.
paragraphs.translationZh: 42. 消费者越来越担心向科技公司提供个人信息以获得定制产品和服务。

paragraphs.sourceText: 43. The Consumer Technology Association is the sponsor of the annual Consumer Electronics Show.
paragraphs.translationZh: 43. 消费者技术协会是年度消费电子展的赞助商。

paragraphs.sourceText: 44. Many consumers wonder about the necessity of having their fitness monitored.
paragraphs.translationZh: 44. 许多消费者想知道监测自己健康状况的必要性。

paragraphs.sourceText: 45. The electronic industry is maturing even though no wonder products hit the market.

paragraphs.sourceText: Questions 46 to 50 are based on the following passage.
paragraphs.translationZh: 第 46 至 50 题基于以下段落。

paragraphs.sourceText: The Paris climate agreement finalised in December last year heralded a new era for climate action.For the first time, the world's nations agreed to keep global warming well below 2℃.
paragraphs.translationZh: 去年12月敲定的巴黎气候协议预示着气候行动的新时代。世界各国首次同意将全球变暖幅度控制在2℃以下。

paragraphs.sourceText: This is vital for climate-vulnerable nations. Fewer than 4% of countries are responsible for more than half of the world's greenhouse gas emissions. In a study published in Nature Scientific Reports, we reveal just how deep this injustice runs.
paragraphs.translationZh: This is vital for climate-vulnerable nations.不到 4% 的国家排放了世界一半以上的温室气体。在《自然科学报告》上发表的一项研究中，我们揭示了这种不公正现象的严重程度。

paragraphs.sourceText: Developed nations such as Australia, the United States, Canada, and European countries are essentially climate "free-riders": causing the majority of the problems through high greenhouse gas emissions, while incurring few of the costs such as climate change's impact on food and water. In other words, a few countries are benefiting enormously from the consumption of fossil fuels, while at the same time contributing disproportionately to the global burden of climate change.
paragraphs.translationZh: 澳大利亚、美国、加拿大和欧洲等发达国家本质上是气候“搭便车者”：通过高温室气体排放造成了大部分问题，却很少承担气候变化对粮食和水的影响等成本。换句话说，一些国家从化石燃料的消费中获益匪浅，同时却对全球气候变化造成了不成比例的负担。

paragraphs.sourceText: On the flip side, there are many "forced riders", who are suffering from the climate change impacts despite having scarcely contributed to the problem. Many of the world's most climate-vulnerable countries, the majority of which are African or small island states, produce a very small quantity of emissions. This is much like a non-smoker getting cancer from second-hand smoke, while the heavy smoker is fortunate enough to smoke in good health.
paragraphs.translationZh: 另一方面，还有许多“强迫骑手”，尽管他们几乎没有为这一问题做出贡献，但他们却遭受着气候变化的影响。世界上许多最容易受到气候影响的国家（其中大多数是非洲或小岛屿国家）的排放量都非常小。这很像一个不吸烟的人因二手烟而患上癌症，而重度吸烟者则很幸运能够健康地吸烟。

paragraphs.sourceText: The Paris agreement has been widely hailed as a positive step forward in addressing climate change for all, although the details on addressing "climate justice" can be best described as sketchy.
paragraphs.translationZh: 《巴黎协定》被广泛认为是在解决所有人的气候变化问题上向前迈出的积极一步，尽管解决“气候正义”的细节可以说是粗略的。

paragraphs.sourceText: The goal of keeping global temperature rise "well below" 2~C is commendable but the emissions-reduction pledges submitted by countries leading up to the Paris talks are very unlikely to deliver on this.
paragraphs.translationZh: 将全球气温上升幅度控制在“远低于”2摄氏度的目标值得赞扬，但各国在巴黎会谈前提交的减排承诺不太可能实现这一目标。

paragraphs.sourceText: More than $100 billion in funding has been put on the table for supporting developing nations to reduce emissions. However, the agreement specifies that there is no formal distinction between developed and developing nations in their responsibility to cut emissions, effectively ignoring historical emissions. There is also very little detail on who will provide the funds or, importantly, who is responsible for their provision. Securing these funds, and establishing who is responsible for raising them will also be vital for the future of climate-vulnerable countries.
paragraphs.translationZh: 超过1000亿美元的资金已经投入使用，用于支持发展中国家减少排放。然而，该协议规定发达国家和发展中国家的减排责任没有正式区别，实际上忽略了历史排放量。关于谁将提供资金，或者更重要的是，谁负责提供资金，也没有详细说明。确保这些资金的安全并确定谁负责筹集这些资金对于气候脆弱国家的未来也至关重要。

paragraphs.sourceText: The most climate-vulnerable countries in the world have contributed very little to creating the global disease from which they now suffer the most. There must urgently be a meaningful mobilisation of the policies outlined in the agreement if we are to achieve national emissions reductions while helping the most vulnerable countries adapt to climate change.
paragraphs.translationZh: 世界上最容易受到气候影响的国家对造成他们现在遭受最严重的全球疾病的影响微乎其微。如果我们要实现国家减排，同时帮助最脆弱的国家适应气候变化，就必须紧急有效地动员协议中概述的政策。

paragraphs.sourceText: And it is clearly up to the current generation of leaders from high-emitting nations to decide whether they want to be remembered as climate change tyrants or pioneers.
paragraphs.translationZh: 显然，要由高排放国家的当代领导人来决定他们是否希望被铭记为气候变化暴君或先驱。

paragraphs.sourceText: Questions 51 to 55 are based on the following passage.
paragraphs.translationZh: 问题 51 至 55 基于以下段落。

paragraphs.sourceText: Teenagers at risk of depression, anxiety and suicide often wear their troubles like a neon (霓虹灯)sign. Their risky behaviors--drinking too much alcohol, using illegal drugs, smoking cigarettes and skipping school--can alert parents and teachers that serious problems are brewing.
paragraphs.translationZh: 面临抑郁、焦虑和自杀风险的青少年常常把自己的烦恼表现得像霓虹灯一样。他们的危险行为——过量饮酒、使用非法药物、吸烟和逃学——可能会提醒家长和老师严重的问题正在酝酿之中。

paragraphs.sourceText: But a new study finds that there's another group of adolescents who are in nearly as much danger of experiencing the same psychiatric symptoms: teens who use tons of media, don't get enough sleep and have a sedentary (不爱活动的) lifestyle.
paragraphs.translationZh: 但一项新的研究发现，另一群青少年也面临同样的精神症状：使用大量媒体、睡眠不足、生活方式久坐的青少年。

paragraphs.sourceText: Of course, that may sound like a description of every teenager on the planet. But the study warns that it is teenagers who engage in all three of these practices in the extreme who are truly in jeopardy. Because their behaviors are not usually seen as a red flag, these young people have been dubbed the "invisible risk" group by the study's authors.
paragraphs.translationZh: 当然，这听起来可能是对地球上每个青少年的描述。但该研究警告说，真正处于危险之中的是那些极端地从事这三种行为的青少年。由于他们的行为通常不被视为危险信号，这些年轻人被研究作者称为“隐形风险”群体。

paragraphs.sourceText: "In some ways they're at greater risk of falling through the cracks," says researcher Vladimir Carli. "While most parents, teachers and clinicians would react to an adolescent using drugs or getting drunk, they may easily overlook teenagers who are engaging in inconspicuous behaviors."
paragraphs.translationZh: “在某些方面，他们被忽视的风险更大，”研究员弗拉基米尔·卡利说。 “虽然大多数家长、老师和临床医生会对青少年吸毒或醉酒做出反应，但他们可能很容易忽视那些行为不引人注目的青少年。”

paragraphs.sourceText: The study's authors surveyed 12,395 students and analyzed nine risk behaviors, including excessive alcohol use, illegal drug use, heavy smoking, high media use and truancy (逃学). Their aim was to determine the relationship between these risk behaviors and mental health issues in teenagers.
paragraphs.translationZh: 该研究的作者对 12,395 名学生进行了调查，并分析了九种危险行为，包括过量饮酒、非法吸毒、大量吸烟、大量使用媒体和逃学。他们的目的是确定这些危险行为与青少年心理健康问题之间的关系。

paragraphs.sourceText: About 58% of the students demonstrated none or few of the risk behaviors. Some 13% scored high on all nine of the risk behaviors. And 29%, the "invisible risk" group, scored high on three in particular: They spent five hours a day or more on electronic devices. They slept six hours a night or less. And they neglected "other healthy activities."
paragraphs.translationZh: 大约 58% 的学生没有或很少表现出危险行为。大约 13% 的人在所有九种危险行为上都得分很高。 29% 的“隐形风险”群体在三项得分上尤其高：他们每天在电子设备上花费五个小时或更多。他们每晚睡六个小时或更少。他们还忽视了“其他健康活动”。

paragraphs.sourceText: The group that scored high on all nine of the risk behaviors was most likely to show symptoms of depression; in all, nearly 15% of this group reported being depressed, compared with just 4% of the low-risk group. But the invisible group wasn't far behind the high-risk set, with more than 13% of them exhibiting depression.
paragraphs.translationZh: 在所有九种危险行为上得分较高的群体最有可能表现出抑郁症状；总体而言，该群体中近 15% 的人表示患有抑郁症，而低风险群体中只有 4% 的人患有抑郁症。但隐形群体并不落后于高风险群体，其中超过 13% 的人表现出抑郁症。

paragraphs.sourceText: The findings caught Carli off guard. "We were very surprised," he says. "The high-risk group and low-risk group are obvious. But this third group was not only unexpected, it was so distinct and so large--nearly one third of our sample--that it became a key finding of the study. "
paragraphs.translationZh: 这一发现让卡莉措手不及。 “我们非常惊讶，”他说。 “高风险组和低风险组是显而易见的。但这第三组不仅出乎意料，而且如此独特、如此庞大——几乎占我们样本的三分之一——以至于它成为这项研究的一个关键发现。”

paragraphs.sourceText: Carli says that one of the most significant things about his study is that it provides new early-warning signs for parents, teachers and mental health-care providers. And early identification, support and treatment for mental health issues, he says, are the best ways to keep them from turning into full-blown disorders.
paragraphs.translationZh: 卡利说，他的研究最重要的事情之一是它为家长、教师和心理保健提供者提供了新的预警信号。他说，早期识别、支持和治疗心理健康问题是防止其发展为全面疾病的最佳方法。
